Amended 2026-08-20: SpanMappingAccumulator (CRIT-153) was removed and OtelCorrelationAccumulator collapsed into a plain field copy (CRIT-152); CircuitBreakerAccumulator gained a recursive analyze_transcript entry point (CRIT-062); SchemaExtractorAccumulator was redesigned around a generic $schema/$id detector and pluggable validator registry with a tri-state result (CRIT-063); HookActivityAccumulator was reworked to consume a dedicated HookExecutionEvent instead of scanning transcript JSON (CRIT-139/140); AttributionAccumulator gained a by_agent bucket and by_subagent now keys on the new subagent_role field (CRIT-147/149); PermissionModeAccumulator (previously implemented with zero bound acceptance criteria) now has a dedicated test task (CRIT-172/173).

tasks.title: Embedded Schema Extraction with Pluggable Validator Registry and Tri-State Results

tdd_steps.failing_test: Add test_schema_extractor_generic_detection_and_validator_registry to test_accumulators.rs: turn 0's entry.text contains an embedded `{"$id":"spec@1","purpose":"x"}` block, with a SchemaValidator registered for schema_id "spec@1" that returns true from validate() -- expect a SchemaCitation{schema_id:"spec@1", turn_index:0, result: SchemaValidationResult::Valid}. Turn 1's text contains `{"$schema":"changeset@1","foo":1}`, with a registered validator for "changeset@1" that returns false -- expect result: Invalid. Turn 2's text contains `{"$id":"eval-report@1","bar":2}` with NO registered validator for that id -- expect result: UnrecognizedSchema. Also update the 4 existing `.is_valid`-based assertions already in this file (currently around lines 589, 633, 637, 684) to check `.result == SchemaValidationResult::Valid` / `SchemaValidationResult::Invalid` instead, since SchemaCitation.is_valid no longer exists after this task.
tdd_steps.expected_failure: Fails to compile: SchemaCitation still has a boolean is_valid field (not result: SchemaValidationResult), and SchemaValidator/SchemaValidationResult do not exist yet; the 4 pre-existing .is_valid assertions also fail to compile once the field is renamed.
tdd_steps.implementation: In crates/lumen-model/src/schema.rs: remove `is_valid: bool` and `summary: Option<CompactString>` from SchemaCitation; add `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub enum SchemaValidationResult { Valid, Invalid, UnrecognizedSchema }` and add `pub result: SchemaValidationResult` to SchemaCitation in its place. Export it from crates/lumen-model/src/lib.rs by changing `pub use schema::SchemaCitation;` to `pub use schema::{SchemaCitation, SchemaValidationResult};`. In crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/schema_extractor.rs: add `pub trait SchemaValidator: Send + Sync { fn schema_id(&self) -> &str; fn validate(&self, payload: &serde_json::Value) -> bool; }`. Change SchemaExtractorAccumulator to `{ pub validators: Vec<Box<dyn SchemaValidator>>, pub extracted: Vec<SchemaCitation> }` (Default still derives cleanly -- an empty Vec needs no bound on its element type). Add a private `fn extract_json_blocks(text: &str) -> Vec<serde_json::Value>` that scans text for every unconsumed `{`, and for each attempts to locate its matching `}` by walking forward tracking brace depth (ignoring braces inside unescaped-`"`-delimited string literals so embedded JSON strings containing `{`/`}` don't desync the count), then tries `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>` on the resulting substring; keeps only successfully-parsed values that are JSON objects containing a string-valued `$schema` or `$id` key, and advances the scan past the consumed closing brace so a successfully-parsed block's own nested braces are not re-scanned as spurious separate blocks. Rewrite `update(&mut self, entry: &CanonicalTurn)`: if entry.text is Some, call extract_json_blocks on it (entry.text is the only field scanned per CRIT-063 -- tool_results.truncated_output stays out of scope, matching pre-amendment behavior); for each parsed block compute `schema_id = block.get("$id").or_else(|| block.get("$schema")).and_then(|v| v.as_str())`, skip the block if None; look up a validator in self.validators whose `schema_id()` equals it -- if found, `result = if validator.validate(&block) { Valid } else { Invalid }`; if none registered, `result = UnrecognizedSchema`; push `SchemaCitation { schema_id: CompactString::new(schema_id), turn_index: entry.turn_index, result }`. `finalize(self) -> Vec<SchemaCitation>` returns self.extracted unchanged. Export `SchemaValidator` alongside `SchemaExtractorAccumulator` from crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/mod.rs. engine.rs's existing `schema_extractor: SchemaExtractorAccumulator` field/wiring needs no change: both the old and new shapes expose `EntryAccumulator<Output = Vec<SchemaCitation>>` via `.update(turn)`/`.finalize()`, and `SchemaExtractorAccumulator::default()` still constructs cleanly with an empty validators registry (meaning every schema block encountered during process_transcript reports UnrecognizedSchema until a future task registers Lumen's own 5 known-schema validators -- registering real Draft-07 validation for those 5 IDs remains out of scope per the spec's own non_goals).

tasks.title: CircuitBreakerAccumulator::analyze_transcript Recursive Stall Detection Tests

tdd_steps.failing_test: Add test_circuit_breaker_analyze_transcript_recurses_into_subagents: build a parent CanonicalTranscript whose own turns produce 2 consecutive same-agent-pair SubagentSpawn rounds (no stall), and whose subagents field contains one child CanonicalTranscript whose own turns produce 3 consecutive same-agent-pair rounds (a real stall, its own turn_index relative to the CHILD's turn list). Call CircuitBreakerAccumulator::analyze_transcript(&parent). Assert: report.stalls has exactly 1 entry (the child's, turn_index unchanged -- not renumbered against the parent), report.max_observed_rounds == 3 (the maximum of parent's 2 and child's 3, not their sum), and report.tripped == true (recomputed after merging, since the parent's own 2 rounds alone would not trip). Also add test_circuit_breaker_analyze_transcript_flat_no_subagents asserting analyze_transcript on a transcript with an empty subagents field produces output identical to calling update() per turn then finalize() directly on a fresh accumulator -- analyze_transcript is a strict superset behavior when there is nothing to recurse into, not a divergent one.
tdd_steps.expected_failure: Fails to compile: CircuitBreakerAccumulator::analyze_transcript does not exist yet.
tdd_steps.implementation: Add to crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/circuit_breaker.rs: `impl CircuitBreakerAccumulator { pub fn analyze_transcript(transcript: &lumen_model::CanonicalTranscript) -> CircuitBreakerReport { let mut acc = CircuitBreakerAccumulator::default(); for turn in &transcript.turns { acc.update(turn); } let mut report = acc.finalize(); for subagent in &transcript.subagents { let sub_report = CircuitBreakerAccumulator::analyze_transcript(subagent); report.stalls.extend(sub_report.stalls); report.max_observed_rounds = report.max_observed_rounds.max(sub_report.max_observed_rounds); } report.tripped = report.max_observed_rounds > 2; report } }`. Stalls are appended in encounter order (the parent's own stalls first, then each subagent's stalls in transcript.subagents order) -- a flat concatenation, no dedup or reorder, per CRIT-062. report.tripped MUST be recomputed after the merge loop, not reused from the parent-only finalize() call, since a subagent-only stall can trip the merged report even when the parent alone does not. This is a new associated function only -- CircuitBreakerAccumulator remains one of CRIT-LUMEN-060's 18 in-loop EntryAccumulators via its existing unchanged update()/finalize(), still called per top-level turn inside AnalyticsEngine::process_transcript's loop. Wiring AnalyticsEngine to prefer analyze_transcript's recursive output over the current flat per-turn-loop result for AnalysisReport.circuit_breaker is explicitly out of scope for this task -- no acceptance criterion requires that engine-level change.

After finalize(): one cluster has canonical "view_file" (count 5, sorted first by -count) with variant "veiw_file" (count 2); "grep" (count 3) is its own cluster with no variants (since "grpe" fails the len<5/threshold=1 test at distance 2); "grpe" and "bash" are singleton clusters. typo_call_count == 2 (only veiw_file's count), typo_rate == 2.0/12.0.

In update(): for each call in entry.tool_calls, increment counts[call.tool_name]; add entry.tool_calls.len() to total_tool_calls once per turn. Write a private `fn levenshtein(a: &str, b: &str) -> usize` using standard O(len_a*len_b) dynamic programming (no new crate dependency -- strsim/levenshtein are not in the workspace Cargo.toml). In finalize(): collect counts into a Vec<(CompactString, usize)>, sort by (Reverse(count), name); walk the sorted list with a visited BTreeSet; for each unvisited name, start a new cluster (canonical = name), mark visited, then scan the REMAINING sorted list in order and assign each still-unvisited candidate as a variant of this cluster (marking it visited) iff 0 < levenshtein(canonical, candidate) <= threshold where threshold = 1 if candidate.len() < 5 else 2; push the finished cluster (ToolCluster { canonical, variants: Vec<(CompactString, usize)> }). Compute typo_call_count as the sum of variant counts across all clusters, and typo_rate = typo_call_count as f64 / total_tool_calls as f64 (0.0 if total_tool_calls == 0).
